circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and micrometases are sensitive to uracil plus tegafur (UFT) and that the chemosensitivity of CTCs and micrometasteses can be evaluated using a novel micrometasasis model featuring Lewis Lung Carcinoma (LLC) cells tagged with the LacZ gene and a hygromycin resistance gene (hyg R).
circulating tumor cells and early micrometastatic cells in the lung are sensitive to oral UFT administration, and that oral UFT administration may be effective for inhibiting micrometastatization.
micrometases and circulating tumor cell are sensitive to uracil/tegafur and that this drug may be used to inhibit micrometasis formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemosensitivity of circulating tumor cells and pulmonary micrometastatic cells to UFT as evaluated using the LacZ gene-tagging technique.
the development of novel methods for detecting micrometastatic tumor cells and for evaluating the effectiveness of anticancer drugs in the treatment of micrometasis.
the development of a new model of micrometasis formation and its application to the study of chemosensitivity of micrometasias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oral administration of the UFT is an effective treatment for the prevention of the formation of micrometases and the reduction of circulating tumor cells in a murine model of lung cancer.
the chemosensitivity of micrometatases is dependent on the stage of micrometatasis formation and the dose of anticancer agent administered.
UFT is a promising agent for the prevention of metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the micrometastatic tumor cells in the early phase of growth in the lung and circulating tumor cells in peripheral blood are sensitive to UFT, and that long-term oral administration with minimal toxic side effect is effective in preventing micrometastase formation.

we have established a new metastasis model using a LacZ-transfector system and that this system is very effective for evaluating the efficacy of chemotherapeutic agents against metastasis formation in vivo.

the micrometastatic phase of the tumor is sensitive to chemotherapy, and that this is an effective time to intervene with drugs.
